claims.text: The MgAlCuZnGd alloy has a density below 6 g/cm³.
The as-cast MgAlCuZnGd alloy is metastable.
The as-cast alloy contains a supersaturated solid solution with minor inhomogeneities and minimal precipitate formation.
Moderate-temperature annealing accelerates Mg diffusion in the non-equilibrium alloy.
Accelerated Mg diffusion initiates spinodal decomposition.
Spinodal decomposition is followed by precipitation of nano- to micrometer-scale Mg-rich intermetallic phases.
The Mg-rich intermetallic phases create compositional gradients and localized galvanic cells.
The precipitates serve as nucleation sites for protective mixed oxides during subsequent high-temperature exposure.
Precipitate-induced mixed-oxide formation produces a more continuous and adherent oxide scale.
Annealing will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast condition.
Annealing will shift the corrosion potential and reduce the corrosion rate relative to the as-cast condition.
Thermally treated samples will exhibit distinct DSC exotherms corresponding to transformation events.
Annealing at approximately 300°C under an inert atmosphere is expected to produce the proposed transformation.
Thermal treatments above approximately 350°C or outside inert or controlled atmospheres may induce alternative phase transformations.
TEM/EDS can test whether annealing produces Mg-rich precipitates and increased compositional inhomogeneity relative to the as-cast control.
The proposed comparison uses as-cast samples as a control for calibrated thermally annealed samples.
